svg.title: OneX Hub final architecture and Transaction History application flow
svg.desc: The diagram shows OneX Hub, Spool, storage-hosted micro-frontends and Thread chunks, the Bobbin fallback service, session service, Apigee and legacy backend, followed by the end-to-end Transaction History search, results, details and receipt flow.
svg.text: OneX Hub — Final Architecture + Application Flow
One shared Hub · independently published MFEs · reusable Thread UI · governed Spool configuration
React UI + frontend workflow + state + API orchestration
Browser downloads approved JavaScript, CSS and assets
No authentication, session, business API or database responsibility
MFEs ARE BROWSER BUNDLES — NOT APPLICATION CONTAINERS
Synthetic identity and session in the current POC
Production backend owns data and database
Enterprise edge must replace or confirm
TRANSACTION HISTORY APPLICATION FLOW — WHAT RUNS AFTER THE MFE IS MOUNTED
The MFE owns client workflow and state; Thread renders reusable controls; the backend remains authoritative.
owns client workflow, state, navigation and API orchestration
owns reusable UI implementations and design consistency
owns authorization, business rules and data
Spool connects them through governed routes, bundle versions, capabilities, operation keys and Thread references.
CURRENT POC: synthetic identities and data · Bobbin is the temporary server boundary
Target: Cloud Run Hub + Cloud Storage/S3 CDN + enterprise session + Apigee + backend
